headline: Jet stream peaked at 12-14 km (25.1 m/s measured); GFS differed most at 10-12 km.
findings: Measured winds increased from 17.6 m/s at 8-10 km to a peak of 21.7 m/s at 12-14 km, then decreased to 4.3 m/s by 18-20 km.
The jet stream core was located between 12 and 14 km altitude, with a maximum measured wind of 25.1 m/s.
GFS model winds were closest to measured at 12-14 km (23.8 vs 21.7 m/s) and 16-18 km (6.5 vs 6.3 m/s).
The largest absolute difference was at 10-12 km, where GFS under-predicted the mean wind by 3.5 m/s (17.5 vs 21.0 m/s).
GFS also under-predicted at 8-10 km by 1.7 m/s and over-predicted at 14-16 km by 2.5 m/s.
anomalies: GFS data has only one sample per altitude band, making statistical comparison unreliable.
GFS shows a secondary wind increase at 20-22 km (7.3 m/s) not present in measured data (no measurements above 20 km).
Measured wind at 14-16 km drops sharply (11.5 m/s) compared to 12-14 km (21.7 m/s), indicating a narrow jet core.

headline: Jet stream at 10-14 km, peak 25.1 m/s measured; GFS off most at 10-12 km (-3.5 m/s)
findings: Jet stream core is in the 10-14 km band: measured means of 21.0 m/s (10-12 km) and 21.7 m/s (12-14 km), with the flight maximum of 25.1 m/s at 12-14 km.
Winds drop off sharply above the core: 11.5 m/s mean at 14-16 km, 6.3 m/s at 16-18 km, and 4.3 m/s at 18-20 km - roughly a quarter of jet strength by 18 km.
GFS captures the overall profile shape (peak at 12-14 km, 23.8 m/s; weakening aloft), but each GFS band is a single sample (n=1) versus 9-14 measured points per band.
Best agreement is at 16-18 km (+0.2 m/s); measured winds never exceed 8.1 m/s above 16 km, so drift aloft is minimal.
Measured data ends at 20 km; above that only GFS exists (7.3 m/s at 20-22 km, 4.8 m/s at 22-24 km) and cannot be verified against the flight.
anomalies: Largest model-measured discrepancy is at 10-12 km: GFS reads 17.5 m/s versus a measured mean of 21.0 m/s, underestimating the jet's lower flank by 3.5 m/s (~17%).
GFS overestimates 12-16 km by 2.1-2.5 m/s, biasing the jet core stronger and slightly broader on its upper side than measured.

GFS and measured disagree on where the jet is strongest relative to 12 km: GFS implies a sharper peak at 12-14 km (23.8) with a weak 10-12 km (17.5), while measurements show a broader, flatter jet of ~21-22 m/s across 10-14 km.
No measured wind data above 20 km despite the 8-24 km query range; the 20-24 km GFS values are unvalidated and should not be trusted for burst-altitude drift planning.
GFS n=1 per band means band averages hide within-band shear; the measured max-minus-mean spread (e.g., 25.1 vs 21.7 at 12-14 km) suggests gradients the model sample may miss.
